title: The Quality hub shows two named halves and only the tiles you may use
why: An assessor-facing area must be easy to find your way around without training.
before: Signed in as Master Admin. The company is set up as one that performs inspection (Marketplace → Company business capabilities).

steps.expect: The page heading reads "Quality & Accreditation" with the line "Two halves: the everyday quality work you touch during jobs, and the accreditation registers an assessor asks for."

steps.do: Look at the two tabs at the top.
steps.expect: Two tabs: "Everyday quality" and "Accreditation registers".

steps.do: Open "Everyday quality".
steps.expect: Tiles: Complaints & appeals, Client acceptance, Customer satisfaction, Items & samples, Hold & witness points, Evidence review, Nonconformity workspace.

steps.do: Open "Accreditation registers".
steps.expect: Tiles: Equipment & calibration, Method library, Decision rules, Controlled documents, Retention schedule, Data & information control, Risks & opportunities, Competence & authorisation, Impartiality, Disclosure consent, Internal audits, Management review, Confidentiality, Site entry documents, Identity documents, SLA targets.

steps.do: Take a screenshot of both tabs.
steps.expect: Screenshots saved for the record.

steps.expect: The "Nonconformities" register opens and lists records.

steps.do: Take a screenshot.
steps.expect: Screenshot saved.

steps.do: Take screenshots.
steps.expect: Screenshots saved.

title: Record a complaint the day it arrives and acknowledge it
why: ISO/IEC 17020 §7.5: the clock runs from the day a complaint arrives, and the acknowledgement date is the first thing an assessor checks.
before: Use records whose title starts with "TEST –" so they are easy to find and close afterwards. Signed in as a Coordinator. A test client exists.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals.
steps.expect: Heading "Complaints & appeals"; buttons "Published description" and "Record one"; a register with columns Ref, Received, From, About, Ours?, Outcome, Decided by, Told, State.

steps.do: Click "Record one".
steps.expect: Heading "Record a complaint".

steps.do: What is it? = "Complaint — dissatisfaction with our work or conduct"; Received on = today; How it reached us = E-mail; Who from = Client; Their name = "TEST Ravi"; E-mail = test@example.com; Which client = your test client; Subject = "TEST – report sent late"; What they told us = "Report issued 8 days after inspection".
steps.expect: All fields accept the values.

steps.do: Click "Record it".
steps.expect: A complaint page opens with a reference like CMP-2026-…, the subject in the heading, and tabs Overview · Handle · History.

steps.do: Open the "Handle" tab. Under "1 · Acknowledge" set Acknowledged on = today, How = "replied by e-mail the same day", click "Record it".
steps.expect: Message: "Acknowledged. That is the first date an assessor looks at."

steps.do: Go back to Complaints & appeals.
steps.expect: The new row shows Received = today and State open.

title: Decide, tell the complainant and close a complaint
why: A complaint is only resolved when someone not involved decides it and the complainant is told — the step most bodies miss.
before: The TEST complaint from the previous case exists and is acknowledged. Signed in as Master Admin (by default only an administrator holds "Decide complaints and appeals"). You were NOT the inspector on that job.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open the TEST complaint → "Handle" tab.
steps.expect: Sections 1 · Acknowledge (done) to 7 · Close are listed.

steps.do: Under "2 · Is it ours to answer?" choose "Ours to answer — it concerns our inspection activities" and click "Save".
steps.expect: Message: "Recorded: Ours to answer — it concerns our inspection activities."

steps.do: Under "3 · Investigate" fill "What we found" and "Root cause"; click "Save findings".
steps.expect: Message: "Saved."

steps.do: Under "4 · Decide" choose Outcome "Not upheld — we found no fault", write the reasons in "The decision and the reasons for it", click "Record the decision".
steps.expect: Message: "Decision recorded."

steps.do: Under "5 · Tell the complainant" set "Written to them on" = today, How = "e-mail to TEST Ravi"; click "Record it".
steps.expect: Message: "Recorded that the complainant was told, and when."

steps.do: Under "7 · Close" click "Close CMP-…".
steps.expect: Message: "Closed."

steps.do: Go back to the register.
steps.expect: The row shows Outcome = Not upheld, Decided by = your name, Told = today's date, State closed.

title: A complaint with an empty subject and description is refused
why: An entry that says nothing proves nothing to an assessor.
before: Signed in as a Coordinator.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → "Record one".
steps.expect: The form opens.

steps.do: Leave Subject and What they told us empty and click "Record it".
steps.expect: The browser stops you and points at the empty required field.

steps.do: Type a single space in Subject and a single space in What they told us; click "Record it".
steps.expect: Message: "A complaint needs a subject and a description — an entry that says nothing proves nothing." No complaint is created.

steps.do: Go back to the register.
steps.expect: No new row was added.

title: Someone who took part in the inspection tries to decide the complaint
why: §7.5.4: the decision must be made by somebody not involved in the original work.
before: A TEST complaint naming, under "Which team member", the person you are signed in as (or naming a job you inspected). The complaint is acknowledged and marked "Ours to answer".

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open the TEST complaint → Overview tab.
steps.expect: A section "Who may not decide this" lists your name.

steps.do: Handle tab → "4 · Decide": choose Outcome "Upheld — the complaint was justified", write reasons, click "Record the decision".
steps.expect: Refused: "You took part in the inspection this concerns. … the decision must be made by, or reviewed and approved by, somebody who was not involved. Ask a colleague who was not on this work to decide it."

steps.do: Check the register.
steps.expect: Outcome and Decided by are still empty for this complaint.

title: Writing to the complainant before deciding is refused
why: Telling a complainant the outcome before there is one would be a false record.
before: A TEST complaint that is acknowledged but not yet decided.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open it → Handle tab.
steps.expect: Section 4 · Decide shows no decision.

steps.do: Under "5 · Tell the complainant" click "Record it".
steps.expect: Refused: "Decide it before writing to the complainant."

steps.do: Look at the "Told" column in the register.
steps.expect: Still empty.

title: A coordinator cannot record a complaint decision
why: Deciding a complaint is a separate right ("Decide complaints and appeals").
before: A TEST complaint acknowledged and marked "Ours to answer". Signed in as a Coordinator.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open it → Handle tab.
steps.expect: The steps are visible.

steps.do: Under "4 · Decide" choose an outcome, write reasons and click "Record the decision".
steps.expect: Refused: "Deciding a complaint needs the “Decide complaints and appeals” permission."

steps.do: Sign in as Finance and look for the Complaints & appeals tile on the Quality hub.
steps.expect: Finance does not see the tile (Finance holds no complaints module).

title: An upheld complaint cannot close until a corrective action is recorded
why: A decision that says we got something wrong must produce a corrective action.
before: A TEST complaint acknowledged, "Ours to answer", complainant reachable by e-mail. You were not involved.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open it → Handle → "4 · Decide": Outcome "Upheld — the complaint was justified", reasons, "Record the decision".
steps.expect: Message: "Decision recorded. We found fault, so a corrective action is now needed before this can be closed."

steps.do: Record "5 · Tell the complainant" with today's date.
steps.expect: "Recorded that the complainant was told, and when."

steps.do: Under "7 · Close" try to close it.
steps.expect: Refused: "This complaint cannot be closed yet. Still to do: record the corrective action raised. …"

steps.do: Under "6 · Corrective action" click "…or go straight to a corrective action".
steps.expect: A corrective action is raised and linked: "Raised CAPA-… and linked it to the complaint."

steps.do: Return to the complaint and close it.
steps.expect: Now it closes: "Closed."

title: "Not ours" needs a reason (E-13)
why: A complaint turned away with nothing written down cannot be defended later.
before: A TEST complaint about another company's work, acknowledged.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → open it → Handle → "2 · Is it ours to answer?".
steps.expect: Decision list shows: Ours to answer…, Not ours — it concerns somebody else’s work, Ours, but outside inspection activities (e.g. commercial).

steps.do: Choose "Not ours — it concerns somebody else’s work", leave "Why" empty, click "Save".
steps.expect: Refused: "Say why it is not ours to answer, and who should handle it if you know. A complaint turned away with nothing written down cannot be defended later."

steps.do: Type a reason and Save again.
steps.expect: Message: "Recorded: Not ours — it concerns somebody else’s work." The register column "Ours?" now shows it is not ours.

title: Acknowledge and decide clocks: zero, blank and large values
why: The two deadlines are what ISO/IEC 17020 cares about; a zero-day clock would make every complaint late.
before: Signed in as Master Admin. Note the current values first (default 3 and 30 days).

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → section "Our own deadlines, and what we publish".
steps.expect: Fields "Acknowledge within (days)" and "Decide within (days)".

steps.do: Enter 0 in "Acknowledge within (days)" and click "Save".
steps.expect: The browser refuses: the value must be 1 or more.

steps.do: Enter -5 and click "Save".
steps.expect: Also refused by the browser.

steps.do: Enter 365 in "Decide within (days)" and Save.
steps.expect: Saved; the value shows 365.

steps.do: Put both values back to what they were and Save.
steps.expect: Original values restored.

title: Back-dated complaint received at month end counts its clock from the received date
why: The clock runs from arrival, not from when somebody typed it in.
before: Signed in as a Coordinator. Acknowledge clock = 3 days.

steps.do: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → "Record one".
steps.expect: Form opens.

steps.do: Received on = the last day of last month (e.g. 30 Sep 2026); fill Subject "TEST – back-dated" and description; "Record it".
steps.expect: The complaint is created; its sub-heading says it was received on that date.

steps.do: Go back to the register.
steps.expect: Received shows the back-dated date, not today; because more than 3 days have passed without acknowledgement it is shown as late / needing action.

steps.do: Acknowledge it today and close the TEST record afterwards (or leave it marked TEST).
steps.expect: Acknowledged message appears.

steps.do: Who from = Anonymous; tick "They asked not to be named"; leave name, e-mail and phone empty; Subject = "TEST – Ø25 & bold ‘quote’ ₹5,000"; description "line 1 / line 2".

steps.do: Handle tab → acknowledge, mark Ours, decide Not upheld, then try "7 · Close" without recording "Tell the complainant".
